assertion_analysis: Lines 69-73 retain the read result, two-attempt and route checks after filtering config calls; restoring refusal-only fallback loses the independently stubbed head or second attempt and fails those checks.

Lines 251-252 fail if the configured executable is bypassed: the default ssh exits 97 and does not produce the calls file; the four-case reproduction at the previous reviewed head records exactly this failure.
Lines 254-255 fail if Git invokes the wrapper for the wrong host or upload-pack path; the expected argv are fixed independently of the runner result.
Line 256 fails if the runner injects a ConnectTimeout option into a configured wrapper; the calls file is first proved present and lines 254-255 prove that it contains actual Git transport arguments.
Lines 258-263 fail if the core.sshCommand identity or proxy options are discarded or reordered before the executable receives them.

Line 265 fails if ls-remote does not advertise the commit created independently in origin; lines 267-271 fail if fetch returns success without transferring that origin commit into the initially empty destination object store.

No added assertion compares an output solely to an input echoed by the same implementation: the commit expectation is created in the independent origin repository and the fetch assertion probes destination object existence using a separate Git invocation.
